candidates.rationale: IC decays monotonically from 0.0250 (2000) to 0.0010 (2013) - a fading stochastic-range effect, not a turnover or half-life problem (turnover is low, half-life moderate at 19.3d). Widening the shared 21-day window smooths the range measure and also moves away from the archive neighbor's 10-day window (already at rho 0.792, the correlation ceiling risk in this pair).

Stability is only 0.93 with the sole negative year at the tail (2013: -0.0023), a late-window regime break. Working memory already marks window swaps (21d, rho 0.972) and denominator restructures (rho 0.915) on this exact chassis as saturated/collapsed, so those levers are closed. Flipping which extreme anchors the range position (downside support vs. upside rejection) changes the numerator's economic hypothesis without touching the exhausted window/denominator.

The weakest fit-window years (2003:0.0005, 2009:0.0066, 2010:0.0023) are high-volatility periods where a single noisy daily close likely swamps the slow-moving book-per-share fundamental inside the ratio. Smoothing only the price leg denoises the value signal while leaving the well-behaved roe leg and the long (>63d) half-life untouched.

Half-life is a short 13.3 days and IC weakens sharply after 2008 (2009:0.0039, 2010:0.0015), consistent with the well-documented post-2008 decay of short-horizon reversal. Widening only the return-mean window reduces reliance on that decayed effect and also pulls away from the near-ceiling archive neighbor (rho 0.780), which shares the same 10-day return window.

Coverage is 0.934, the closest to the 0.90 floor in this batch, and working memory flags this exact asset_turnover x return-mean family as saturated for decorrelation (window and grafted-leg attempts both failed at rho 0.81-0.85 elsewhere), prescribing a fundamental swap instead. Roa shows near-full coverage (0.987-0.997) on other fundamentals in this batch and is untried in this template.

Stability dips to 0.93 with an isolated negative 2012 (-0.0018) and a short 12.2-day half-life, both consistent with noisy short-horizon reversal dominating the return-mean leg. Widening only that window addresses the decay while leaving the eps/close value leg untouched; a different window than the sibling mutation on parent 693246746bbdc073 (21 vs 42) avoids re-converging this already-close pair (rho 0.780).

IC fades to 0.0016 in 2012 and turns negative (-0.0028) in 2013 - the same late-window decay pattern seen in the other high-low-range factors this round. Shortening only the 'distance from high' lookback makes it more responsive to the faster, more competitive microstructure of the later years, while leaving the volume-rank denominator (shared with the parent, not with any other archive member) untouched.

Highest turnover in the batch (0.294, charged 0.011) and shortest half-life (3.0 days) point to the fast-moving short-vol leg as the main churn source. Working memory explicitly marks the TS_DELTA window as saturated (w=5 and w=10 both archive_subtree) and names the volatility-ratio leg's own windows as the untried lever, so only the short TS_STD denominator window is widened to smooth the churn.

Nearest archive correlation is 0.792, one tick from the 0.80 ceiling, and working memory states this exact asset_turnover x return-mean family is saturated at every window (rho 0.81-0.85) even with a grafted leg, prescribing a fundamental swap. Roe also fixes this parent's low coverage (0.941, second-lowest in the batch) and its worst single-year drawdown (2012: -0.0063).

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

  12. Multiplying ($high-$low) directly by TS_MEAN($return,5) inside a fundamental cross barely fails cheap_screen (|t| 0.98), while subtracting a separately CS_RANKed TS_MEAN($return,5) from a separately CS_RANKed product clears easily (fitness 4.834).
